question_text: Must you use a turn signal when changing lanes?

answers.A: Yes, you must signal before every lane change
answers.C: Only when other vehicles are nearby
answers.D: No, signals are only for turns at intersections

explanation: You must give a proper turn signal before changing lanes so drivers around you know your intention. Signaling lowers the risk of a side collision. Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot before moving over.

question_text: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at about the same time:

answers.A: The driver on the right must yield to the driver on the left.
answers.B: Both vehicles may proceed at the same time.
answers.C: The driver who signals first has the right-of-way.
answers.D: The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

explanation: An uncontrolled intersection has no traffic signs or signals. The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question_text: What do the colors of traffic signs indicate (red, orange, yellow, etc.)?

answers.A: All colors mean the same thing
answers.B: Each color has a meaning: e.g., red = stop/prohibition, orange = construction, yellow = general warning, green = guide/direction
answers.D: Red means go and green means stop

explanation: Sign colors carry meaning: red signals stop or prohibition, orange marks construction, yellow gives a general warning, and green provides guidance and directions. Recognizing the color tells you what to expect. React to each color appropriately.

question_text: What are the main aids for a blind person when traveling?

answers.B: A white cane or a wheelchair
answers.C: A red cane or a trained guide dog
answers.D: A white cane or a trained guide dog
